nodes.title: the Duthsol signature
nodes.statement: The Duthsol system concerns objects called opalmis. There are exactly 5 of them: keldsib, duthzam, hobfex, iskxil, qenxil. One operation is written -. One relation is written <~, read as "covers".

nodes.title: the Duthsol combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x - y for every pair of opalmis is fixed by the table of the first operation. The pairs standing in the <~ relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all opalmis x and y, x - y is again a opalmi.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all opalmis x, y, z: (x - y) - z = x - (y - z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all opalmis x and y: x - y = y - x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a opalmi duthzam with duthzam - x = x - duthzam = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a opalmi keldsib with keldsib - x = x - keldsib = keldsib for every x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all opalmis x and y: if x <~ y and y <~ x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all opalmis x, y, z: if x <~ y and y <~ z then x <~ z.

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some opalmi x admits no opalmi y for which x - y and y - x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = keldsib, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every opalmi x: x - x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = hobfex, value = qenxil, read straight from the tables.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all opalmis x, y, z: if x - y = x - z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every opalmi x: x <~ x.

nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all opalmis x, y, z: if x <~ y then (z - x) <~ (z - y) and (x - z) <~ (y - z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

nodes.title: qenpyr opalmis
nodes.statement: A opalmi x is called qenpyr when x - x = x.

nodes.title: opalmis that siblum
nodes.statement: Two opalmis x and y are said to siblum when x - y = y - x.

nodes.title: brarast collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of opalmis is brarast when x - y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the espafex of a opalmi
nodes.statement: The espafex of a opalmi x is the collection of opalmis y for which x <~ y holds.

nodes.title: the sibisk
nodes.statement: The opalmi duthzam is called the sibisk of the system. It is the unique opalmi that leaves every opalmi unchanged under -.

nodes.title: the zamlorn
nodes.statement: The zamlorn of the system is the collection of opalmis that siblum with every opalmi.

nodes.title: the tarnsol
nodes.statement: The tarnsol is the collection of all qenpyr opalmis.

nodes.title: the nakyuk of a opalmi
nodes.statement: The nakyuk of a opalmi x, written [x], is the smallest brarast collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a hobsol
nodes.statement: A opalmi f is a hobsol when f <~ y holds for every opalmi y, that is, when the espafex of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: gelpyr opalmis
nodes.statement: A opalmi x is gelpyr when x - x equals the sibisk.

nodes.title: the vexisk of a opalmi
nodes.statement: The vexisk of a opalmi x is the number of opalmis in its nakyuk [x].

nodes.title: the duthpon
nodes.statement: The duthpon of the system is the collection of opalmis whose vexisk is largest.

nodes.title: grixhob pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct opalmis x and y form a grixhob pair when x <~ y and y <~ x both hold, that is, when each lies in the espafex of the other.

nodes.title: the sibisk is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one opalmi e with e - x = x - e = x for every opalmi x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every opalmi unchanged.
Then e - f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e - f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the sibisk lies in the zamlorn
nodes.statement: The sibisk siblums with every opalmi.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the sibisk and x any opalmi.
Then e - x = x and x - e = x.
So e - x = x - e, which is what it means to siblum.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the zamlorn.

nodes.title: the zamlorn is brarast
nodes.statement: If x and y both siblum with every opalmi, then so does x - y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the zamlorn and let z be any opalmi.
Then (x - y) - z = x - (y - z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each siblums with everything.
So x - y siblums with z, and the zamlorn is brarast.

nodes.title: the nakyuk of a opalmi is brarast
nodes.statement: For every opalmi x, the collection [x] is brarast.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under -.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the nakyuk is contained in every brarast collection
nodes.statement: If S is brarast and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a opalmi is qenpyr exactly when its vexisk is one
nodes.statement: x - x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x - x = x then {x} is already closed under -.
So [x] = {x} and the vexisk is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x - x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the vexisk divides the number of opalmis breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every opalmi x, the vexisk of x divides 5.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = hobfex, reach = 4, size = 5, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the nakyuk of a zamlorn opalmi stays in the zamlorn
nodes.statement: If x lies in the zamlorn then every opalmi of [x] lies in the zamlorn.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The zamlorn is brarast.
[x] is the smallest brarast collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the zamlorn is one.

nodes.title: the tarnsol is brarast
nodes.statement: If x and y are both qenpyr then so is x - y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be qenpyr.
The claim asks whether (x - y) - (x - y) returns x - y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: espafexs are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the espafex of x, then the espafex of y is contained in the espafex of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x <~ y and let z satisfy y <~ z.
Transitivity gives x <~ z.
So every member of the espafex of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one hobsol
nodes.statement: No two distinct opalmis can both be hobsols.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f <~ h, since h is any object, and h <~ f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: no grixhob pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct opalmis lie in each other's espafex.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every opalmi lies in the zamlorn
nodes.statement: Every pair of opalmis siblums.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The zamlorn is defined by sibluming with everything.
The claim is that x - y = y - x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.
